title: 3.5.22 Lab: Destructure 3 Fields From an Object
description: Unpack three fields in one statement, use the bare names, and rewrite a function to destructure its parameter. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Build an object with three fields
steps.instructions: Create an object with at least three properties, for example a title, a cost, and a quantity.

steps.title: Unpack into three variables
steps.instructions: Destructure three of its properties into variables in one statement, using braces on the left of the equals sign.

steps.title: Use the bare names
steps.instructions: Use the three variables (no dot, no object name) to build and print a sentence.

steps.title: Destructure a parameter
steps.instructions: Write a function called describe that takes one options object and destructures two or more of its keys directly in the parameter list, then returns a string from the bare names.

requirements.title: object destructuring used
requirements.description: Unpacks with a brace pattern. Help: 3.5.19 (Destructuring)

requirements.title: parameter destructured
requirements.description: A function parameter is a brace pattern. Help: 3.5.19 (Destructuring)

requirements.title: describe takes one object and uses its fields
requirements.description: describe({ title: "Pen", quantity: 10, cost: 2 }) returns text containing Pen and 10, and the function takes exactly one parameter. Help: 3.5.20 (Example: Destructure a Parameter)
requirements.hint: describe takes ONE parameter (an object) and unpacks title and quantity from it with braces in the parameter list. Return a string that uses both names.

checks.expr: typeof describe === 'function' && describe.length === 1 && (s => s.includes('Pen') && s.includes('10'))(String(describe({ title: 'Pen', quantity: 10, cost: 2 }))) && (s => s.includes('Cup') && s.includes('4'))(String(describe({ cost: 1, quantity: 4, title: 'Cup' })))
checks.fail: describe should take one object and use its fields: describe({ title: "Pen", quantity: 10, cost: 2 }) must give text that contains Pen and 10.
